text:
andrew: quick note from today's sync — we keep hitting a bad interaction between immediate demote and rare long-tail cursors. idea: introduce a prefetch_compensation_ledger that records denied/soft-denied prefetches and can later reimburse tenant credits when cluster is underutilized. thoughts?

meera: ledger makes sense to preserve fairness without chasing noise. how would entries be represented? tiny immutable events per-prefix?

andrew: yes, append-only events: {tenant, prefix, denied_amount, reason, ts}. consumers (reconciler) periodically aggregate and issue compensatory credit grants when slab spare > threshold.

pablo: careful about growth. need bounded retention and aggregation windows. maybe keep 1h raw and rollup to 24h aggregates. also cap max compensation per-tenant per-hour.

meera: correctness check: if we later reimburse and those credits are applied while old cursors are still active, could we re-introduce RAWR? need a safety gate.

andrew: agreed. reimbursement should be marked as "compensatory" and only usable for non-blocking prefetch budget (no write pins). also reconcile can consult slab.can_reweight(tenant) before applying. if can_reweight==DEFER, we delay reimbursement and emit metric.

tara: sounds ok but ops wants deterministic auditing: we should emit ledger_tx_id and ensure idempotent apply. also provide an endpoint to list pending compensations for a tenant.

pablo: rollout: feature flag to enable ledger write-only (record denies but don't reimburse), run for a week to validate volumes and heuristics, then enable small reimbursements in canary slabs.

andrew: another complementary idea: a demote_grace window — when a slab decides to demote, instead of immediately reducing credits, it first enters a grace window (e.g., 8s) where it rate-limits prefetch and increases sampling for active cursors. if grace expires and pressure persists, then do full demote. prevents oscillation.

meera: prefer grace+ledger combo. grace prevents thrash; ledger preserves fairness long-term. what signals start the grace timer? sustained evict_rate spike + demote_throttle_count > X?

andrew: propose trigger = (evict_rate > spike_thresh) && (demote_recent_count < demote_limit) to avoid repeated grace abuse. we also add hysteresis: require stability for Y secs before exiting grace early.

pablo: metric wishlist: ledger_denied_total, ledger_compensated_total, grace_entered_count, grace_expiry_count, grace_aborted_on_pins. add alert if uncompensated_ledger_bytes grows > 100MB.

tara: ops runbook: FF off, run ledger-only for 7d, verify per-tenant compensation volume < 1% of tenant_quota, then enable reimbursements at 0.1% ramp. emergency flag to freeze reimbursements and drain ledger.

ops-bot: created alert candidate "ledger_uncompensated_growth" (severity: p2) and "demote_grace_persist" (severity: p1).

andrew: short pseudocode for reconciler: ```
read ledger window W -> aggregate per-tenant denied_amount
for tenant, amt in aggregates:
  if slab.spare>comp_thresh and slab.can_reweight(tenant)==OK:
    apply_compensatory_credits(tenant, min(amt, per_tenant_cap))
  else:
    emit("compensate_deferred", tenant)
```

meera: small nit: ensure ledger events are compacted deterministically so auditors can recompute totals easily. e.g., rollup by tenant+prefix+minute with monotonic ids.

andrew: agreed. I'll draft RFC with: ledger schema, retention/rollup policy, reconcile algo, grace window state machine, metrics, ops playbook, and SLO acceptance criteria. will ping SRE and product for QoS caps. thanks all. :thumbsup:
